match.reason: No bank point teaches just the contrast that mechanical waves need a medium while electromagnetic waves can cross a vacuum; the closest points cover only one side (sound) or go broader (the full spectrum) or at a different depth (wave properties in Physics).

draft.title: Mechanical and electromagnetic waves
card: A wave carries energy from place to place. A medium is the matter a wave travels through, such as air, water or a solid.
needs a medium. Its energy passes from particle to particle, as in sound or a wave on water.
can travel through a vacuum, which is empty space with no matter. Light, radio waves and X-rays are examples.
Sunlight reaches Earth across empty space, so light is electromagnetic. Sound cannot cross a vacuum, because there are no particles to pass it on.
draft.remember: Mechanical waves need a medium. Electromagnetic waves can travel without one.

a.q: Why can sound not travel through a vacuum?
opts: There are no particles to pass the energy on
There is no light to carry the sound
Sound waves are too weak to cross space
Sound is an electromagnetic wave that fades
a.why: Sound is a mechanical wave, so its energy passes from particle to particle. A vacuum has no particles. Sound is not electromagnetic, so the last option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what a mechanical wave needs.

b.q: Mia watches a firework display from a hill in Bendigo. She sees the flash first and hears the bang a moment later. Which statement is correct?
opts: Light is electromagnetic and sound is mechanical
Light is mechanical and sound is electromagnetic
Both light and sound are electromagnetic waves
Both light and sound need air to travel through
b.why: Light is an electromagnetic wave and sound is a mechanical wave that needs a medium, here air. The two kinds of wave are different, so the other options mix them up.
b.clue: Which of the two could cross space from the Sun?

a.best: There are no particles to pass the energy on

b.best: Light is electromagnetic and sound is mechanical
